title: Request log scrub & guardrails - API + Console demo - Boreal Tech
meeting_header:
Date: 2027-06-21
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Recording: enabled
Platform: Zoom
Agenda: quick demo of request storage toggles, logging redaction, PII scrub, and Optimize recommendations for cost/latency trade-offs
summary: Redwood AE + SE ran through API and Console options for controlling request storage and logs. Focus on selective redaction, policy-driven ejection, storeless endpoints, and how Optimize suggests batching/quantization for cost. Customer concerned about SOC 2, KMS key flow, and ability to run a short pilot with synthetic PII and latency targets.
topics: API: storeless vs stored request endpoints
Console: request storage toggles and policy presets
PII handling: ephemeral storage, auto-redact, regex rules vs ML detection
Optimize recommendations: batching, quantization, cache TTL
Security: KMS, SSO/SAML, audit logs, retention windows
action_items: Maya Lin - Send SOC 2 summary, KMS integration notes, and security pack - due 2027-06-24
Ethan Park - Share demo recording and console screenshots of retention toggles - due 2027-06-22
Priya Natarajan - Provide sample PII schema and retention policy currently used - due 2027-06-25
Devon Hall - Confirm pilot scope (10k requests/day, 30 day) and success metrics - due 2027-06-23
next_steps: Redwood to send security artifacts and architecture diagram
Schedule 60-min pilot kickoff and baseline latency run
Customer to provide sample prompts and PII examples for redaction tuning
Follow-up call week of 2027-06-28 to review pilot plan
transcript:
00:00 Maya Lin (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call?
00:05 Rita Gomez: Rita here, CTO at Boreal.
00:07 Devon Hall: Devon, product.
00:09 Priya Natarajan: Priya, secops.
00:11 Maya Lin: Great, Ethan and I will run through the request-storage toggles and redaction demo, show API behavior and Console presets. We have about 45 minutes so we'll keep it focused.
00:28 Ethan Park (SE): Cool, I'll share my screen. Uh, first slide is the high level: storeless endpoints that never persist request payloads, and stored endpoints where you can set retention windows and redaction rules.
00:45 Samir (Engineer): Quick question — is storeless truly zero-storage, like no logs at all?
00:49 Ethan Park: Yeah like, storeless means payloads aren't written to request storage; ephemeral traces for debugging are ephemeral and TTL'd, and we also have an opt-in debug mode. But audit logs still note request IDs and outcome codes, not full text.
01:05 Priya Natarajan: And encryption at rest? Keys managed by us?
01:09 Maya Lin: We support customer-managed keys via KMS / HSM. The keys for request storage are optional and can be rotated. We'll send the KMS flow doc.
01:20 Devon Hall: On the Console, show us how we create a policy that redacts PII automatically — regex vs ML detection, what's the default?
01:27 Ethan Park: By default we ship a set of regex and heuristic detectors for common PII (SSNs, credit card patterns, emails). You can add ML detectors for names/entities, and chain rules — regex first, then ML. There's also an allowlist/denylist for fields.
01:45 Maya Lin: Note: the ML detector can have false positives, so for sensitive production you'd normally mix both and run a brief tuning pass with your sample prompts.
01:58 Ethan Park: Showing Console now, top right: Request Storage -> Toggle: Store requests (ON/OFF). If OFF, that maps to storeless API endpoints. If ON you get retention window slider and redaction rules.
02:20 Ethan Park: (demo clicking) Here's policy presets: Compliance-30d (30 day retention, strict PII redaction), Dev-7d (7 day, relaxed), NoStore. You can also create custom policies and attach them per-route.
02:39 Priya Natarajan: Can policies be enforced per API key or per model?
02:43 Ethan Park: Per API key, per route, and you can pin a policy to a model version too.
02:53 Samir (Engineer): How about KV cache and prefix caching, does that leak PII back into prompts?
02:58 Ethan Park: Good question. Cache keys are hashed; we never persist raw prompts in KV. However if you do prefix caching with user messages, you'd have to scrub text before caching or use per-customer cache namespaces.
03:20 Rita Gomez: Our compliance team will ask about audit logs — need to see immutable audit trails of policy changes and who accessed what.
03:28 Maya Lin: Yes, Console audit logs record policy edits, user actions, and we can ship those to your SIEM via syslog or S3. We include before/after diffs for policy changes.
03:45 Devon Hall: And SSO?
03:47 Maya Lin: SAML/SSO supported, RBAC controls for fine-grained roles.
03:54 Ethan Park: Back to redaction: here's a demo sample. I'm going to send a request containing a fake SSN and a name.
04:08 Ethan Park: (runs API) Raw request: "Hi, my name is John Alvarez, SSN 111-22-3333, please summarize my medical case".
04:18 Ethan Park: Console shows the stored request scrubbed to "Hi, my name is [REDACTED_NAME], SSN [REDACTED_SSN], please summarize my medical case" behind the scenes.
04:32 Priya Natarajan: Does redaction change the prompt enough to ruin model accuracy?
04:38 Ethan Park: Sometimes — there's a tradeoff. For structured extractions we recommend token-preserving masking (e.g., replace with token-length placeholders) or field-level extraction where you store the PII separately in an encrypted store and pass a reference. Optimize can also flag when redaction causes a quality drop and suggest alternative model variants.
05:05 Devon Hall: You mentioned policy-driven ejection earlier — what is that?
05:10 Ethan Park: Policy-driven ejection is where requests that match a rule (e.g., contains PCI data) get automatically ejected from storage or sent to a secure vault. You can set synchronous ejection for immediate removal or async ejection for batched processing.
05:27 Rita Gomez: We need to know about retention windows — can we set per-route minima? For example, financial routes must be 90 days, others 7 days.
05:36 Maya Lin: Yes per-route and global minima/ maxima. There's also a console policy compliance checker that flags routes that violate org-wide policies.
05:49 Samir (Engineer): Is there an API to programmatically change retention in case of incidents?
05:54 Ethan Park: Yes, full infra API — you can change policy via API and we log the action. For high-security accounts we can require multi-person approval flows for changing retention.
06:08 Priya Natarajan: Any considerations for private deployments / VPCs?
06:12 Maya Lin: In Private mode we deploy control plane in your VPC and data plane can be on-prem or in your cloud. You retain full network control and keys. Some customers run dedícated capacity with strict egress rules.
06:28 Devon Hall: Cost impact — storing requests vs storeless — what's the rough delta?
06:33 Maya Lin: It depends. Storing and retaining text adds storage and indexing costs. Our back-of-envelope: storing text with 30 day retention is roughly X% more than storeless for high QPS workloads. Optimize will give a per-route recommendation — e.g., use storeless for chat preview, store for compliance routes.
07:00 Ethan Park: (shared spreadsheet) Here's sample numbers: storeless saves ~20-40% on token storage-related costs at our sample volumes; retention length scales linearly with S3 and index costs.
07:17 Devon Hall: On Optimize, can it automatically suggest batching and quantization by route?
07:22 Ethan Park: Yes, Optimize analyzes latency SLOs and request size distribution. It suggests batching sizes, quantization profiles and cache TTLs. You can apply suggestions with one click in Console.
07:35 Rita Gomez: We have a 300ms p95 latency SLA for customer-facing search. If we enable redaction or prefix masking will that push us over?
07:44 Ethan Park: Redaction happens pre-store, not on the inference path by default. For synchronous redaction we add ~15-45ms depending on the ML detector. Regex-only is sub-10ms. For tight SLAs we recommend regex at the critical path and async ML detectors as a background job.
08:10 Priya Natarajan: Can we run your redaction on-prem during pilot to avoid sending PII to your hosted detectors?
08:15 Maya Lin: Yes, we can run a local redaction worker in your VPC or on-prem as part of Private deployment. That worker can be configured to never leave your network.
08:28 Samir (Engineer): About logging — sometimes I see names of models or internal queue ids in logs. Can those be masked?
08:34 Ethan Park: We can obfuscate internal identifiers and only surface friendly route names in the audit stream. There is a sanitization pipeline that can be configured.
08:45 Devon Hall: Competitors may push automatic ML-only redaction, which is simpler but less explainable. We need auditability.
08:53 Maya Lin: Exactly — we emphasize explainable redaction chains and diffs in audit logs.
09:05 Ethan Park: Quick demo of API toggle. Endpoint /v1/generate?store=false — hits storeless path. If store=true you get storage-id and it's subject to retention policy linked to your API key.
09:28 Rita Gomez: For legal holds, can we pin certain requests beyond the normal retention?
09:33 Maya Lin: Yes, you can mark requests as legal-hold; they move to a secure hold bucket and require an explicit release flow. All holds are logged.
09:44 Devon Hall: How granular can redaction rules be? For example, redact free text email addresses but keep domain names?
09:50 Ethan Park: You can write field-level rules, domain-preserving masks, regex with capture groups, or a post-redact transformer that swaps out values preserving structure.
10:05 Priya Natarajan: If we use per-customer KMS keys, how does key access work for Redwood?
10:10 Maya Lin: You can give Redwood a limited key-encrypt/decrypt role or hold keys exclusively. For hosted mode we typically do envelope encryption where Redwood stores wrapped keys; you control rotation. For Private you keep keys fully. We'll attach the KMS flow doc.
10:33 Samir (Engineer): Let's talk about a pilot — we want a 30 day pilot with 10k requests/day, test redaction and retention changes, and measure latency and cost.
10:42 Maya Lin: Sounds good. We can provision a dedicated sandbox with a lower retention default, provide a sample Optimize report, and run a baseline 48-hour latency run.
11:00 Ethan Park: We'll also run a synthetic PII test suite to tune ML detectors — we need your sample prompts.
11:10 Devon Hall: Question on ejection: if something is ejected and moved to vault, is it immutable or can we rehydrate?
11:17 Ethan Park: Vaulted requests are archived and access-controlled; you can restore a copy for forensic analysis but that action is logged and requires permission.
11:30 Rita Gomez: Ok let's talk timeline. We're up for a pilot next week.
11:35 Maya Lin: We'll send security pack and proposed pilot scope today. Can we reconvene next Tuesday for a kickoff?
11:42 Priya Natarajan: Yes Tuesday early am works.
11:45 Ethan Park: Closing recap: we'll share SOC2, KMS notes, console screenshots, pilot scope. Customer to share sample prompts and PII definitions.
11:55 Devon Hall: Thanks everyone.
12:00 Meeting end.

Notes on transcript: occasional transcription artifacts (e.g., "dedicate" vs "dedicated") and speaker overlaps were left as-is to preserve meeting feel. Some technical terms transcribed as "K-B cache" in one snippet then corrected in context.
